newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna stocks tumble as investors lose faith.
newsitem.headline: Vienna stocks tumble as investors lose faith.

text.p: Austrian shares dropped over one percent to end near the day's low on Friday, weighed down by weaker international leads and selling ahead of Boehler's half-year earnings, dealers said.

The session, marked by low turnover and widespread investor pessimism, was also under pressure as investors waited for a firm response from the EA-Generali-led consortium as to whether it would make an offer for Creditanstalt before a deadline at midnight today, they said.

The ATX index of 21 blue chips lost 11.67 points, or 1.13 percent, to 1,021.59 after trading between 1,020.80 and 1,033.26. Of its constituents, 16 fell, four gained and one was unchanged by the close.

Shortly before the market closed, the bourse announced it had suspended trade in Creditanstalt ordinary and preferred shares, as well as in EA-Generali ordinary shares pending an important announcement.
"The suspension in the shares helped bruise sentiment further. There's a lack of confidence among investors that they'll get a bid together," said a trader at an Austrian bank.

A source close to the negotiations over the privatisation of Creditanstalt told Reuters that Die Erste has left the Austro-Italian-German group bidding for the state's 70 percent voting stake and that EA-Generali would submit its own offer for the flagship bank.
"The consortium wanted to go it alone," the source said.

High-grade steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm was the ATX's worst performer. It tumbled over six percent to a new year low of 759 schillings as investors worried second-half results -- due on Monday -- could be worse than expected, a dealer said.
Wolford was the biggest gainer, adding on 0.81 percent to 2,490 schillings.
For the upcoming week, the market would keep its eye on U.S. interest rate policy. A change of more than 25 basis points could shake the bourse, a trader said.
The all-share Vienna bourse index fell 0.91 percent to 400.16, while the September ATX future lost 11.1 points to 1,022 on turnover of 276 contracts.
